newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand keeping close eye on foreign share sales.
newsitem.headline: Thailand keeping close eye on foreign share sales.

text.p: The Thai finance ministry and the Bank of Thailand are jointly monitoring heavy foreign selling that has battered the local stock market, a senior official said on Monday.

"Looking at the market, if it does not recover today, the finance minister may have to find ways to discourage foreign selling," the ministry's permanent secretary Chatumongkol Sonokul told reporters without elaborating.
The Thai stock market was down sharply by 5.51 percent or 55.40 points to 949.49 at 0822 GMT.

Brokers blamed heavy selling by foreign firms, especially of banking and finance stocks, for the sharp slide on the stock market. Among key negative factors were dim prospects for further interest rate cuts, central bank restrictions on foreign fund inflows and the poor outlook for the Thai economy.
Chatumongkol attributed foreign investor sales to fears that banks' profits may be squeezed this year and concerns over the sluggish property sector.

He also disagreed with the idea that the government ought to ask private Thai mutual funds to enter the market to buy and curb further falls. "All mutual funds' primary concern must be to maintain the benefits of their unit trust holders," Chatumongkol said.
